optionAudit.label: ①
optionAudit.intent: polarity reversal — uniformity enforcement as the opposite of appreciating differences
optionAudit.temptingBecause: sounds like a plausible group-management measure that could reduce conflict; 'standards of behavior' superficially relates to group functioning
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: the passage argues that taking others' perspectives and appreciating differences enables open communication; enforcing uniform standards suppresses exactly the differences the passage says should be appreciated

optionAudit.label: ②
optionAudit.intent: half-truth / lexical anchor — echoes 'a diverse emotion vocabulary' from the opening definition
optionAudit.temptingBecause: verbatim lexical overlap with 'emotion vocabulary' in the first sentence rewards surface matching
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: vocabulary is only one component of the ability; the sentences immediately preceding the blank are about perspective-taking, not lexicon size, and 'a simple increase in vocabulary size' is explicitly reductive, so it cannot summarize what creates open communication and constructive resolution

optionAudit.label: ③
optionAudit.intent: concept substitution — conflict avoidance confused with constructive conflict resolution
optionAudit.temptingBecause: uses the passage's own anchor word 'conflict' and avoidance intuitively sounds like a path to group harmony
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: internally contradictory with the completed sentence itself: avoiding conflicts cannot 'promote constructive conflict resolution', and the passage's example is a conflict being worked through, not avoided

optionAudit.label: ④
optionAudit.intent: correct answer — abstraction of the removed span 'Appreciation of differences'
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: none — entailed by 'take the perspective of the other group members and understand why they are reacting in a certain manner' and is a faithful, appropriately abstracted paraphrase of the source span

optionAudit.label: ⑤
optionAudit.temptingBecause: the passage does mention accommodating 'their own needs', so a partial reader may recall the individual-needs mention
optionAudit.decisiveFlaw: the passage says members accommodate their own needs AS WELL AS the needs of others (i.e. cooperate); prioritizing individual over group goals reverses the cooperation claim and cannot yield improved group functioning
